title: Online Unity, C#, Python & Scratch Tutor — Ihor Sivochka
description: 1-on-1 online programming & game dev mentoring for kids and teens: Unity & C#, Python, Minecraft, Scratch, CS. €20 / ~$22 (1000 UAH) per 60 min.
heading: Personal 1-on-1 Mentoring in Unity, C#, Python & Computer Science
intro: I am Ihor Sivochka (Figarist)—a practicing indie game developer, Master of Education in Computer Science, and creator of live EdTech web platforms. My flagship track is 1-on-1 Unity and C# mentoring for kids and teenagers (building 2D/3D games, enemy AI, multiplayer, and portfolio projects from scratch). I also teach Python (including via Minecraft), Scratch for ages 6+, and school computer science. Personal 1-on-1 mentoring with no group slides or mass classes.
audience: Children and teenagers ages 6–17 worldwide (Ukraine, Europe, UK, USA, Canada, Israel).
language: 1-on-1 Zoom mentoring · 60 min · Worldwide (EU, US, CA, UA)
availability: Weekly schedule slots are limited. Message on Telegram to check availability and align on goals.
project_note: Every project grows around the student's ideas—from first playable prototypes to multi-mechanic 3D games. Pace and scope match age and experience.
steps: We align with parents on Telegram (student age, time zone, hardware, goals) and reserve a regular weekly slot. The first paid 60-minute session starts right into practice.
We work live 1-on-1 on the student's own project—progressing from simple mechanics to C# architecture, physics, AI behavior, or multiplayer networking.
I explain why the code works, teach independent debugging, and adapt the pace without templated group presentations.
proof: Learn with a builder shipping real games and EdTech tools
proof_text: Instead of textbook theory, students learn with an active developer whose live games and web apps run right on this domain: Dish of Chaos (Unity 6 WebGL), 3D Club Studio, OGCruncher Web Audio DSP, LEGO WeDo 2.0 Catalog (597 guides), and Quiet Class (Bouncy). Credentials include Unity Junior Programmer, Unity Essentials, a Master's degree in Education, and 18 independent 5/5 reviews on BUKI and the Ukrainian Tutors Association.
game: Play my game Dish of Chaos
questions: How much do individual lessons cost and why is this 1-on-1 mentoring?

The fixed rate is €20 for families in Europe / ~$22 USD for the US and Canada (or 1000 UAH) per 60-minute 1-on-1 session. You work directly with an active indie game developer, Master of Computer Science Education, and EdTech creator—not mass group courses or junior instructors. Weekly slots are limited so every student's codebase receives focused attention.
Is there a free trial lesson?

Initial parent consultation on Telegram (discussing age, goals, hardware readiness, and choosing a track) is free. The first full 60-minute hands-on lesson and project kickoff is paid at the standard rate (€20 / ~$22 / 1000 UAH).
Which age and track is the best starting point?

Ages 6–9 usually start best with Scratch to build algorithmic thinking. Ages 9–12 are ideal for Python (including through Minecraft) or transitioning into Unity. Ages 10–17 thrive in the flagship Unity & C# track, building real 2D/3D games for their portfolio.
Can students join from Europe, the US, Canada, or Israel?

Yes, most students join online from across Europe, North America, Israel, and Ukraine. Lessons are held on Zoom in a reserved weekly slot matching your local time zone (available in Ukrainian or Russian; international terminology in English).
What computer setup is required?
Unity, Python, and Minecraft require a Windows or Mac computer/laptop with Zoom, screen sharing, and software installation access. Scratch works on a computer or tablet.
How do I book a weekly slot?
Message @Figarist on Telegram with the student's age, country/time zone, preferred track (Unity/C#, Python, Scratch, CS), prior experience, and convenient hours.
How do I pay for lessons?
Payment details are listed in the conditions above.

questions: How much do Unity & C# lessons cost and why is it 1-on-1 mentoring?

Each 60-minute individual session costs €20 / ~$22 USD (1000 UAH). You work 1-on-1 with a Unity Junior Programmer & Unity Essentials certified developer and Master of Computer Science Education, with the entire hour dedicated to your child's game architecture and C# code.
Can I start Unity without knowing C#?

Yes. We begin with the editor and simple controlled objects, then introduce C# variables, conditions, loops, methods, and classes directly inside real game mechanics so the student understands every line rather than copy-pasting.
Can a student bring an existing game project?
Yes. We review the existing project, organize its architecture, and define clear next engineering steps without unrealistic completion guarantees.
Can students join from abroad?
Yes, lessons run online via Zoom screen sharing, scheduled to fit time zones in Europe, the UK, USA, Canada, and Israel.
What computer is needed for Unity?
A Windows or macOS computer/laptop capable of running Unity Hub, a code editor, and Zoom (8–16 GB RAM recommended for 3D projects; verified before booking).
